answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the weighted attestation graph, so voting influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than raw identities. A sybil cluster may look dense internally, like a karst hollow, yet its sparse external cut gives it low conductance. Mixing and min-cut bounds limit how much stationary trust can cross that boundary; thus the cluster’s aggregate voting weight stays constrained, even if a plume of fabricated accounts inflates its apparent size.
